He uses the word "cache" twice, and never once in the context that is important: every major secure implementation these days runs the content through a cached front-end before it is served. Any admin worth his salt isn't serving that content up on Apache server; he's serving it up on a Tomcat instance running in front of an Apache server, which is doing all the caching, encapsulating, and encrypting. It isn't just the protocol that is different these days... it's the whole shebang. And waxing philosophical about "whingers" and their apples/oranges doesn't take the air out of those sails, because they're valid points.
